$comment: Guards the invariants of install-dns-failover.sh that keep a bad dnsmasq.conf from taking DNS down. Evaluated by scripts/check-policies.mjs (checkFileRules; comment lines ignored). See docs/security/SECURITY-AI.md, section 'The installer'.

required.why: the installer must run under `set -eu` so a failed `dnsmasq --test` aborts before the config is installed
the reviewed config must be checked by a standalone `dnsmasq --test --conf-file="$config"` command before it is installed (not as an if/negated condition, which `set -e` does not abort on)
the installed config must be validated with systemd-helper checkconfig and a dnsmasq restart, with a failure branch

the running /etc/dnsmasq.conf must be backed up on every run: the copy to "$backup" is the rollback target, so it must be an unindented command of its own, not inside an `if` or a list, and --remove-destination keeps it from writing through a symlink saved by an earlier run
the first-install original keeps its own path, so the per-run copy can never replace it
the per-run rollback copy keeps its own path in the root-only directory, apart from the first-install original

forbidden.why: `set +e` lets a failed `dnsmasq --test` fall through to the install
a failed `dnsmasq --test` must not be ignored
the installer installs only reviewed local files and downloads nothing
the installer runs as root and must not shell out to sudo
`dnsmasq --test` must be a standalone command; as a condition or in a list a failure does not abort the installer under `set -e`

everyAfter.why: the reviewed config must be installed only after `dnsmasq --test` passes
the backup must exist before the config is replaced
checkconfig must run on the installed config
the backup is restored only after the new config was installed

followedWithin.why: a restore of the backup must restart dnsmasq and then exit non-zero
a restore of the backup must restart dnsmasq so the old config is live again
the first-install original must be written only when it does not exist yet, as a file or as a symlink that dangles from the backup directory, so an already-modified file never replaces it
the once-only `if` must hold nothing but the copy of the original, so the per-run copy after its `fi` happens on every run
the failure branch must first print which config it restores, so the message survives a failed restart
